LLM-based role-playing chatbots have been developed to simulate speakers of different personal attributes and linguistic styles so as to provide more immersive interaction with users.

we implement two metrics to assess the role-playing models. The first metric, named Simulation Score, concentrates on the fidelity of simulation, measuring the similarity between the real utterances and the agent-generated utterances for the same speaker. The second metric, named Distinction Score, measures how dissimilar the agent-generated utterances are for different roles.

We introduce two metrics: (a) Simulation Score, which evaluates the alignment of agent‑generated utterances with actual utterances from the target speaker, and (b) Distinction Score, which measures the differences among utterances generated by the same agent model when simulating various speakers.
